By @sec-covariance-matrix,
the estimated standard error of $\hmean_{\text{ML}}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\HSE{\hmean}
&= \sqrt{\sb{\inv{\oinf(\hmean, \hvarpar)}}_{11}}
&& \text{(estimated standard error from the inverse information)}\\
&= \sqrt{\frac{\hvarpar}{n}}
&& \text{(first diagonal entry of the inverse information)}\\
&= \frac{\hsdpar}{\sqrt{n}}
&& \text{(square root of a quotient)}
\end{aligned}
$$

which shrinks in proportion to $1/\sqrt{n}$
(@fig-hers-se-by-n).

::: {#fig-hers-se-by-n}

```{r}
se_mu_hat <- function(n, sigma) sigma / sqrt(n)
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_function(fun = se_mu_hat, args = list(sigma = sigma_hat)) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_log10(
    limits = c(10, 10^5), name = "Sample size",
    labels = scales::label_comma()
  ) +
  ggplot2::ylab("Standard error of mu-hat (mg/dL)")
```

Standard error of $\hmean_{\text{ML}}$ as a function of sample size,
with $\sdpar = \hsdpar_{\text{ML}}$

:::
